text:
maria: Quick proposal — introduce a new SKU called 'FlexCredits' for mid-market customers to handle variable usage without lots of one-off contract exceptions. Sketch below and looking for scope / launch criteria input.

alex: high level — how is this different from the existing burst packs and reserved commits?

maria: short: simpler mapping to tokens + controlled rollover + softcap/overflow pricing. Aimed at customers who don't want long commits but need predictable unit economics and optional priority routing. Example pricing sketch: 
```
FlexCredits SKU v0.1
- Starter: 10,000 credits / month @ $500 (rollover up to 30% of monthly allocation)
- Growth: 50,000 credits / month @ $2,000 (rollover up to 50%)
- Overage: $0.06 / credit until softcap; after softcap, overflow rate $0.10/credit OR automatic fallback to lower-tier model if opted-in
- Mapping: 1 credit ~ 5k tokens (configurable per customer)
- Add-on: Priority routing (+15% on the SKU price) for Dedicated/Dedicated-like throughput
- SLA: apply existing Dedicated latency SLOs when priority routing enabled
```

jamal: engineering notes — we can wire this into quota service as "bucket + rollover" and reuse existing overage billing path. Main work: billing window rollover logic, per-customer mapping (credit->token), and expose per-route toggle for priority routing. Also need policy for softcap enforcement (bill-first vs throttle-first).

sophie: sales POV — must be a single-line value prop for AEs, plus a short FAQ about rollover and how credits map to tokens. They will ask: can credits be split across routes?

ben-sales: sales input — customers ask for: 1) simple predictability; 2) ability to prioritize a subset of routes; 3) rollover so they don't lose credits on slow months. I have 3 pilots in mind: Delve (analytics), Marketly (SaaS), NodeLoop (platform) — all asked for something between burst and commit.

alex: product tradeoffs to call out for PRD: complexity for billing vs. revenue stickiness, runway for pilots before GA, and whether priority routing should be automatic or an opt-in add-on. My recommendation: bill-first for overage (clear incents), and provide throttling as an opt-in safety. Also require fallback-to-cheaper-model option for high-cost spikes.

maria: proposed launch criteria: 1) implement quota + rollover in billing and console UI; 2) priority routing toggle in Console and API; 3) 3 signed pilots with usage baseline and acceptance tests; 4) docs + AE one-pager + FAQ; 5) run evals on pilot prompts to ensure quality delta when falling back.

jamal: rough delivery estimate — we can scope an MVP in 6 weeks if we: A) reuse current billing overage infra, B) postpone cross-customer cache/Routing optimizations, and C) limit UI to a single page for SKU management. If we expand mapping granularity or automate model-fallback, add 3–4 weeks.

sophie: marketing/sales ask — need a short commitable phrase for pitch and a clear pricing table. I'll draft the AE one-pager once PRD is out. :thumbsup:

ben-sales: I'll line up the pilots if we agree to the pricing guardrails and the rollover rules (no more than 50% rollover for GA).

maria: thanks all. Next steps: I'll draft PRD today and tag @jamal for tech spec sync tomorrow 10:00am PT. Anyone object to billing-first overage + opt-in throttling? :eyes:

alex: no objections from me. :+1:

jamal: OK, billing-first makes the implementation path clearer. I'll bring a short tech plan to the sync.

maria: great — I'll post the PRD link in this thread when ready.
